payload.task_text:
Hi there, the Fall 2014 semester just wrapped up and I need to prepare a summary for the department. Could you pull together an overview of all the courses from that term?

Please look up all courses that ran in Fall 2014 and gather the following for each: the course name, course code, total number of students, enrollment count, number of assignments, and the average points possible across all assignments (rounded to 1 decimal). If a course has no assignments, record Avg Points Possible as 0.0. If an individual assignment has a null or zero points_possible, include it in the count but treat its points as 0 when computing the average.

Create an Excel file called Semester_Summary.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets.

The first sheet should be called "Course Overview" with columns: Course Name, Course Code, Total Students, Enrollments, Assignments, Avg Points Possible. One row per course, sorted alphabetically by course name.

The second sheet should be called "Summary" with columns Metric and Value, containing these rows: Total Courses, Total Students (sum of all course total_students), Total Enrollments (sum of all enrollment counts), Total Assignments (sum of all assignment counts), Average Assignments per Course (rounded to 1 decimal).

Also create a PowerPoint presentation called Semester_Summary.pptx in the workspace. It should have:

A title slide with "Fall 2014 Semester Summary" as the title.

An overview slide showing the summary statistics (total courses, total students, total enrollments, total assignments, average assignments per course).

One slide for each course showing the course name as title and its details (course code, total students, enrollments, assignments, average points possible).

A final "Key Takeaways" slide identifying the largest course by student count, the smallest course by student count, and the course with the most assignments. For each, include both the course name and the specific numeric value (e.g. "Largest: CCC-2014J with 2498 students").

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, combine the three small reads for each concrete Fall 2014 course and freeze deterministic extrema before either writer starts.

The main agent calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true), retains exactly the returned courses whose full name contains Fall 2014 or whose code ends in 2014J, and freezes every literal ID/code/name and reported total_students. It then instantiates one Explore prompt per retained course.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 7 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per literal Fall 2014 course below:

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Course Explore agent for course_id=2 (AAA-2014J): issue canvas_list_assignments(course_id=2, include_submissions=false) and canvas_get_course_grades(course_id=2, page=1, per_page=1) natively in parallel. Return {course_id:2,course_code:"AAA-2014J",course_name,total_students,assignment_ids,assignment_count,points_possible_values,total_enrollments:pagination.total_count,pagination_controls}. Include null/zero assignment points in the returned values, do not fetch enrollment rows, and do not modify Canvas.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Course Explore agent for course_id=4 (BBB-2014J) — same literal recipe, only the course identity substituted.
   3. explore 2 (enterprise-data-analyst 2): Course Explore agent for course_id=7 (CCC-2014J) — same literal recipe, only the course identity substituted.
   4. explore 3 (enterprise-data-analyst 3): Course Explore agent for course_id=10 (DDD-2014J) — same literal recipe, only the course identity substituted.
   5. explore 4 (enterprise-data-analyst 4): Course Explore agent for course_id=14 (EEE-2014J) — same literal recipe, only the course identity substituted.
   6. explore 5 (enterprise-data-analyst 5): Course Explore agent for course_id=17 (FFF-2014J) — same literal recipe, only the course identity substituted.
   7. explore 6 (enterprise-data-analyst 6): Course Explore agent for course_id=21 (GGG-2014J) — same literal recipe, only the course identity substituted.

After Wave 1, the main agent validates one result per frozen course and unique assignment IDs. Compute Avg Points Possible with the task's null/zero rule and requested rounding. Freeze one canonical seven-row Course Overview table and five Summary rows. Compute largest-by-students, smallest-by-students, and most-assignments by running deterministic argmax/argmin over the complete canonical table, using course_code ascending only as a tie-break. Assert each selected row belongs to that table and its metric equals the recomputed extremum. Freeze the three literal takeaway strings; writers may not select or recompute extrema.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): One Coder is the sole writer of Semester_Summary.xlsx in the dynamically resolved task workspace. Create exactly Course Overview and Summary with the exact headers, canonical rows, literal values, sorting and rounding; read both populated ranges back.
   2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 1): One Coder is the sole writer of Semester_Summary.pptx in that workspace. Consume only the frozen canonical course rows, summary rows and three literal takeaway strings. Create exactly ten slides: title, overview, seven course slides in course-name order, and Key Takeaways. Read back all slide titles/text and require every course and each frozen takeaway to occur once.

After Wave 2, the main agent reconciles both artifacts against the same payload, including the deterministic extrema assertions. Do not hard-code expected course names/counts, write to /workspace directly, or dispatch a verification wave.

nodes.text:
Context: You are gathering Fall 2014 semester metrics from a Canvas LMS instance for a department summary report. The Canvas root account is ID 1 ("Open University") with four faculty sub-accounts (IDs 2-5). I have already identified the complete set of Fall 2014 courses — the 7 course IDs below. Your job is read-only data gathering and aggregation only; do not create or modify anything in Canvas.

Courses to analyze (id | name | course_code | total_students as seen in account listings):
- 2 | "Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014)" | AAA-2014J | 365
- 4 | "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014)" | BBB-2014J | 2292
- 7 | "Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014)" | CCC-2014J | 2498
- 10 | "Data-Driven Design (Fall 2014)" | DDD-2014J | 1803
- 14 | "Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2014)" | EEE-2014J | 1188
- 17 | "Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)" | FFF-2014J | 2365
- 21 | "Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)" | GGG-2014J | 749

For EACH of the 7 courses, collect:
1. Total students: call canvas_get_course and use its total_students field (verify against the value above; report the actual returned value).
2. Enrollment count = total number of enrollment records for the course across ALL enrollment types and ALL states. Use canvas_get_course_grades(course_id, per_page=100, page=1), then keep increasing the page number and calling until the response reports pagination.has_more == false. Count every enrollment record returned across all pages. If a page response is truncated or reported as overlong/too large, re-run with a smaller per_page (e.g., 50 or 25) until you can count reliably. Also keep a simple breakdown: how many records are StudentEnrollment vs all other types (TeacherEnrollment / TaEnrollment / DesignerEnrollment / Observer).
3. Assignments: call canvas_list_assignments(course_id) (do not include submissions). Count the assignments. Compute the average of points_possible: sum points_possible over all assignments treating any null/None or missing value as 0 (zero values already contribute 0), divide by the assignment count, and round to 1 decimal place. If a course has zero assignments, average = 0.0. Also note how many assignments had null or zero points_possible.

Deliverable in your final message:
- A compact JSON array with one object per course: {course_id, course_name, course_code, total_students, enrollments, student_enrollments, non_student_enrollments, assignments, null_or_zero_point_assignments, avg_points_possible}
- Plus a summary object: {total_courses, total_students_sum, total_enrollments_sum, total_assignments_sum, avg_assignments_per_course_rounded_1dp}
Keep the final answer to aggregates only — no raw per-record listings.
Collect Fall 2014 course metrics

Create an Excel workbook at exactly this path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-canvas-semester-summary-ppt/workspace/Semester_Summary.xlsx

The workbook must contain exactly two sheets with the exact data below (all values are verified; do not alter numbers).

SHEET 1 — name it exactly "Course Overview" (create the workbook, rename/keep the first sheet as this):
Header row (row 1), columns A–F: Course Name | Course Code | Total Students | Enrollments | Assignments | Avg Points Possible
Then 7 data rows, already sorted alphabetically by course name, starting row 2:

Row 2: Applied Analytics & Algorithms (Fall 2014) | AAA-2014J | 365 | 369 | 6 | 33.3
Row 3: Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Fall 2014) | BBB-2014J | 2292 | 2296 | 6 | 50.0
Row 4: Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014) | CCC-2014J | 2498 | 2501 | 10 | 30.0
Row 5: Data-Driven Design (Fall 2014) | DDD-2014J | 1803 | 1807 | 7 | 28.6
Row 6: Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2014) | EEE-2014J | 1188 | 1191 | 5 | 40.0
Row 7: Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014) | FFF-2014J | 2365 | 2369 | 13 | 69.2
Row 8: Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014) | GGG-2014J | 749 | 752 | 10 | 100.0

Numeric columns (C, D, E, F) must be stored as numbers, not text. Format column F (Avg Points Possible) to display one decimal place (e.g., 0.0 format). Optionally bold the header row.

SHEET 2 — name it exactly "Summary":
Header row (row 1): A1 = "Metric", B1 = "Value"
Then these 5 rows in this exact order and with these exact metric labels:
Row 2: Total Courses | 7
Row 3: Total Students | 11260
Row 4: Total Enrollments | 11285
Row 5: Total Assignments | 57
Row 6: Average Assignments per Course | 8.1
All values in column B must be numeric (8.1 displayed with one decimal).

After writing, read back both sheets to verify contents match exactly, and report the final file path and a brief verification result.
Build Semester_Summary.xlsx

Create a PowerPoint presentation and save it to exactly this path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-canvas-semester-summary-ppt/workspace/Semester_Summary.pptx

Use a clean professional design (any built-in template/theme is fine). The deck must contain 10 slides in exactly this order, with the exact text content below (numbers are verified data — do not change them; write numbers as plain digits without thousands separators):

SLIDE 1 (title slide):
Title: Fall 2014 Semester Summary
Subtitle (optional): Department Overview — Open University

SLIDE 2 (overview of summary statistics), title: Semester Overview
Bullets:
- Total Courses: 7
- Total Students: 11260
- Total Enrollments: 11285
- Total Assignments: 57
- Average Assignments per Course: 8.1

SLIDES 3–9: one slide per course, in this order; each slide's TITLE is the full course name, and it shows these bullet details:

Bullets: Course Code: AAA-2014J | Total Students: 365 | Enrollments: 369 | Assignments: 6 | Avg Points Possible: 33.3

Slide 7 — Title: Environmental Economics & Ethics (Fall 2014)
Bullets: Course Code: EEE-2014J | Total Students: 1188 | Enrollments: 1191 | Assignments: 5 | Avg Points Possible: 40.0
Slide 8 — Title: Foundations of Finance (Fall 2014)
Bullets: Course Code: FFF-2014J | Total Students: 2365 | Enrollments: 2369 | Assignments: 13 | Avg Points Possible: 69.2
Slide 9 — Title: Global Governance & Geopolitics (Fall 2014)
Bullets: Course Code: GGG-2014J | Total Students: 749 | Enrollments: 752 | Assignments: 10 | Avg Points Possible: 100.0

SLIDE 10 (final slide), title: Key Takeaways
Bullets:
- Largest course by student count: Creative Computing & Culture (Fall 2014) (CCC-2014J) with 2498 students
